attribution: PPG derived from USDA FoodData Central nutrition data via lib/fermentable-math.ts: PPG = 46 x (total carbohydrate - fibre) / weight. Fruit is mostly water, so PPG per POUND is low — that is expected and correct, not an error. Ripeness varies these figures substantially.

fermentables.name: Apple (whole)
fermentables.description: Fresh apple. Most of the weight is water, so gravity contribution per pound is modest.
fermentables.usageNotes: Pectin haze is likely — pectic enzyme helps. Add in secondary to preserve aroma.

fermentables.name: Apple Juice / Sweet Cider
fermentables.description: Pressed apple juice, typically SG 1.045–1.050 on its own — enough to ferment straight into cider with no added water.
fermentables.usageNotes: Use preservative-free juice: potassium sorbate or benzoate will stop fermentation dead.

fermentables.name: Raspberry
fermentables.description: Very high fibre and low sugar, so little gravity — you add raspberries for colour and aroma, not alcohol.
fermentables.usageNotes: Typical: 1–2 lb per gallon in secondary.

fermentables.name: Blackberry
fermentables.description: Deep colour and earthy dark-fruit character with minimal gravity contribution.

fermentables.name: Strawberry
fermentables.description: Notoriously fugitive — strawberry aroma fades fast through fermentation. Add late and generously.

fermentables.name: Blueberry
fermentables.description: Higher sugar than most berries; contributes purple hue that often shifts toward grey-blue at beer pH.

fermentables.name: Tart Cherry (Montmorency)
fermentables.description: The classic kriek cherry — acidic and aromatic. Pits contribute a subtle almond/marzipan note over long ageing.

fermentables.name: Sweet Cherry (Bing)
fermentables.description: Sweeter and less acidic than sour cherries; more gravity, less character.

fermentables.name: Peach
fermentables.description: Delicate stone fruit; like strawberry its aroma is easily lost — purée or late addition works best.

fermentables.name: Apricot
fermentables.description: Holds its character better than peach; a traditional lambic fruit.

fermentables.name: Mango
fermentables.description: High-sugar tropical fruit that pairs naturally with thiol-forward hazy IPAs.

fermentables.name: Pineapple
fermentables.description: Tropical and acidic. The base of Mexican tepache; bromelain can thin body and degrade foam proteins.

fermentables.name: Passionfruit
fermentables.description: Extremely aromatic and acidic — small additions carry a long way.

fermentables.name: Guava
fermentables.description: Musky tropical aroma; pairs with the same thiols hop varieties like Sabro throw.

fermentables.name: Banana
fermentables.description: Unusually high sugar for a fresh fruit. The base of East African banana beers (urwagwa, mbege).
fermentables.usageNotes: Very starchy when underripe — use fully ripe or overripe fruit.

fermentables.name: Wine Grapes
fermentables.description: The highest-sugar common fruit — wine grapes at harvest run 20–26 °Brix. Also the basis of Italian Grape Ale.

fermentables.name: Grape Juice / Concentrate
fermentables.description: Pressed grape juice; concentrate is far denser and should be measured by gravity rather than weight.

fermentables.name: Orange Juice
fermentables.description: Citrus juice; acidity drops wort pH noticeably in quantity.
fermentables.usageNotes: Fermented orange juice loses most of its fresh character — zest carries the aroma better.

fermentables.name: Cranberry
fermentables.description: Very tart and tannic; contributes acidity and astringency as much as fruit.

fermentables.name: Pumpkin (fresh/purée)
fermentables.description: Contributes very little gravity and, honestly, little flavour — pumpkin beer character comes mostly from the spices.
fermentables.usageNotes: Roast first for any real flavour, and expect a sticky, filter-clogging mash.

fermentables.name: Raisins
fermentables.description: Dried grapes — water removed, so the PPG is nearly sugar-level. Traditional in Belgian dark strongs and in country wines.

fermentables.name: Dates
fermentables.description: Dense dried fruit sugar with deep caramel and fig character.

fermentables.name: Dried Figs
fermentables.description: High fibre keeps effective extract below dates and raisins, but the flavour is distinctive.
